newsitem.title: ITALY: ITALY RATE RISE UNLIKELY DESPITE STRONG DLR -- PRODI.
newsitem.headline: ITALY RATE RISE UNLIKELY DESPITE STRONG DLR -- PRODI.

text.p: Italy's prime minister Romano Prodi said on Thursday that he sees short term rises in European interest rates, including those in Italy, as unlikely despite the continued high level of the dollar.
In an interview with Milan financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore, Prodi said the dollar's rise had been too rapid, but that for Italy the lira remained strong against most other European currencies.
"I am not preoccupied (by the high dollar), because of the low prices of raw materials and low inflation the general picture does not have to change," he said.

Prodi maintained that no-one thinks Germany is on the point of raising interest rates, and he did not see it economically or politically possible to raise rates in Germany with unemployment running at 11 percent.
